ShouldDisappearFromDoom.maps_to: no sim counterpart; DoomPower is unported
ShouldDisappearFromDoom.rationale: Presentation, and this is the CROSS-BATCH ADJUDICATED verdict on the mechanism (binding rule 3) after two batches disagreed -- recorded as ruled, and independently re-derived before recording. `ShouldDisappearFromDoom` has exactly one reader in the whole game tree: DoomPower.cs:90, and line 90 sits inside the PRIVATE helper `PlayVfx`, which early-returns when the creature has no visual node (DoomPower.cs:82-86). The `flag` it computes is consumed in exactly two places -- `StartDoomAnim(nCreature, flag)` (DoomPower.cs:92) and a Cmd.Wait(0.25f)/Cmd.Wait(1.5f) timing branch (DoomPower.cs:101-111). StartDoomAnim's shouldDie arm (DoomPower.cs:117-134) is `Monster?.OnDieToDoom()`, an AnimDisableUi tween, QueueFreeSafely, a Spine "Hit" trigger, `NCombatRoom.RemoveCreatureNode` (removal of the VIEW node) and an NDoomVfx variant; `OnDieToDoom` is documented at MonsterModel.cs:485-491 as 'Primarily used set up the creature visuals for the Doom vfx', has an empty base body, and its one override (TorchHeadAmalgam.cs:67-79) hides three light nodes. DECISIVE: the kill does NOT consult it -- DoomPower.DoomKill (DoomPower.cs:40-53) is `await PlayVfx(creature); await CreatureCmd.Kill(creature);`, so the Kill is UNCONDITIONAL and outside PlayVfx. The flag therefore gates whether the sprite vanishes with the doom animation, never whether the creature dies or leaves Enemies. Waiver on presentation, matching monster_state_machine N2 and the KinPriest N6 precedent (read the override to the end before verdicting). That the sim has no Doom at all is a secondary observation and is NOT the load-bearing part of this argument.

AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's pool-wide verdict, copied not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation IS construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect (IllusionPower 1 on itself, EyeWithTeeth.cs:30-34) is applied from `__init__` (fogmog.py:31-35). The game applies it from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom (MonsterModel.cs:313-316 is a no-op base, so the override is the whole effect), awaited by CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded inside StartCombatInternal, i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart. Same observable today on all three clauses SHARED-FINDINGS establishes by execution: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the reachable hooks (relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38, relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53, relics/vambrace.py:26-40, relics/paels_legion.py:36-43) all gate on the player and a monster's starting power/block is self-applied with no card; (b) HP-roll inversion -- of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp and only inside revive() (powers.py:2067), never at apply time; (c) roll ordering -- all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-ops (monster_probes.py roll-order). One adaptation: this creature is a MID-COMBAT spawn, so the sim's construction runs inside Fogmog's ILLUSION move and the HP-roll inversion of clause (b) is against CreatureCmd.add's `combat.assign_parity_hp(creature)` (cmds.py:819-827) rather than combat.py:422-442. The clause still holds verbatim and is the shared finding's own worked example: IllusionPower is the ONE constructor-applied power class that mentions max_hp, and only inside revive() (powers.py:2063-2067), never at apply time. Its AfterApplied side effect (MinionPower 1, IllusionPower.cs:66-72) is mirrored in the sim constructor (powers.py:2037-2039). Rule 7: the four relic files and sts2_rl/powers.py named above are NOT hashed by this record (powers.py is hashed only where this record cites it with line numbers).

guards.what: LIVE GAP -- death is not removal. IllusionPower.cs overrides ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath (:108-114) and AfterDeath (:77-90), NOT ShouldDie; the sim ports it onto should_die (powers.py:1566-1570), so an Eye With Teeth never dies and no on_death listener ever fires for it
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 6): both powers are off `should_die`. Neither AdaptablePower nor IllusionPower overrides ShouldDie in C# -- grep the decompiled sources and there is no such member on either. What they implement is `ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath` (AdaptablePower.cs:58-66, IllusionPower.cs:108-116) and `AfterDeath` (:32-39, :76-90), so the death is REAL: Hook.ShouldDie returns true, CreatureCmd.cs:508 computes shouldRemoveFromCombat false, and :519 dispatches Hook.AfterDeath with wasRemovalPrevented FALSE. The sim answered `should_die` False and took the PREVENTED branch, so every listener without a wasRemovalPrevented guard -- Gremlin Horn is one, GremlinHorn.cs:24-32 -- saw the wrong arm. powers.py now carries `should_remove_from_combat_after_death` on both and arms the revive from `on_death`'s `not was_removal_prevented` arm, which is where AfterDeath does it. Pinned by test_glory.py::TestDeathPreventionBranch, which asserts hp 0, retained_after_death, and a single on_death dispatch carrying False on both the Test Subject and an Eye With Teeth.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-28. THE on_death HALF IS CLOSED: cmds.py:30-65's `_resolve_death` now mirrors CreatureCmd.KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition's two arms (CreatureCmd.cs:506-570) -- it dispatches `hooks.on_death` on BOTH, with was_removal_prevented False on the real arm (:519) and True on the prevented one (:566), and it no longer floors the prevented creature at 1 HP. EXECUTED on a killed Eye With Teeth: hp=0, is_dead=True, retained_after_death=True, and the on_death listener fires (relics/gremlin_horn.py has no wasRemovalPrevented guard, matching GremlinHorn.cs:24-32, so it now pays out as the game does). WHAT REMAINS: IllusionPower is STILL ported onto `should_die` (powers.py:1671-1675) where IllusionPower.cs implements only ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath (:108-114) and AfterDeath (:77-90) and NO ShouldDie, so the sim takes the death-PREVENTION arm and two things still diverge: (a) Hook.AfterDeath is dispatched with wasRemovalPrevented TRUE where the game passes false, and (b) the prevented arm never reaches `_strip_powers_after_death` (cmds.py:67-84), so Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath (Creature.cs:668-671, called from CreatureCmd.cs:533 on the real-death arm) never runs. EXECUTED: a Eye With Teeth killed while carrying a player-applied Vulnerable 3 keeps ['illusion', 'minion', 'vulnerable']; the game strips Vulnerable, because it is a non-temporary Debuff and IllusionPower.ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath returns `!(power is ITemporaryPower)` = true for it (IllusionPower.cs:59-66), and keeps only the two Buffs. STILL LIVE and still the same mechanism as relic/gremlin_horn G1 and audit/records/power/illusion.json -- not re-verdicted here. Eye With Teeth is still summoned by Fogmog's ILLUSION move (fogmog.py:93-99, Fogmog.cs:66) in a ported overgrowth NORMAL encounter (rooms.py), so the reachability argument is unchanged.

guards.what: The REVIVE turn: C# splices a MoveState('REVIVE_MOVE', ReviveMove, HealIntent) with FollowUpStateId = StateLog.Last().Id and MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning (IllusionPower.cs:77-90); the sim branches inside the monster's own take_turn (fogmog.py:44-52)
guards.rationale: Same observable sequence: one turn showing a heal intent that restores the creature to full, then back to DISTRACT. The two machine-level side effects of the splice are both inert here -- the FollowUpStateId resolves to DISTRACT_MOVE either way because that is the only move in the log, and the duplicate StateLog entry the splice creates cannot move any weight because EyeWithTeeth has no RandomBranchState at all (EyeWithTeeth.cs:36-43). ShouldAllowHitting (IllusionPower.cs:92-103) is mirrored at powers.py:1572-1575.

guards.what: DistractMove adds 3 Dazed to the targets' DISCARD pile in one CardPileCmd.AddToCombatAndPreview call (EyeWithTeeth.cs:50); the port loops add_to_discard three times (fogmog.py:53-56)
guards.rationale: Same pile, same count, same order (append). The sim's add_to_discard is documented as mirroring AddToCombatAndPreview (cmds.py:1670-1682) and fires on_card_entered_combat per card, which is what the game's per-card AbstractModel registration does; batching three into one call would change nothing a listener can see, because no ported on_card_entered_combat listener reads a count.

It is a telegraph-detail loss, not a behavioural one: take_turn adds the right three cards. Recorded rather than skipped so the hole has a per-unit datum.

guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:422-442), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit's MaxInitialHp is `=> MinInitialHp`, so the range is the single value 6 and no endpoint can be lost; the check is recorded anyway because an off-by-one would turn a one-element candidate list into an empty one and change which ARM of SetUniqueMonsterHpValue runs (NextItem vs NextInt), which is a stream-position difference even when the HP is identical. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [6,6], observed [6,6], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 6 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:78) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
